entries.section: (1) The numbering of the people and the appointment of heads from the tribes

paragraphs.text: After the people came out of the land of bondage (the Book of Exodus), the building of the tabernacle of meeting (the house of God) was among the most important matters and the first of them; that is, God had to set apart a house before the journey began. After the tabernacle was built (Ex 40:17), the Lord spoke to Moses from it, first concerning the laws, the sacrifices and the feasts (Lev 1:1). The second discourse came here, and its time was fixed as the second month of the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt. Since the Book of Exodus had mentioned that the arrival in the wilderness was in the third month of the first year, this discourse with Moses took place eleven months after they reached the wilderness.

After the tabernacle of meeting was built, God always spoke from it, as though He wished to say to everyone who wants to know the voice of God and His will in his life: Come to My Church, for there I will hear you and speak with you as well. This is why we call the Church "the house of God." So if you are seeking God, beloved, do not waste your time; go to His house, speak with Him and listen to Him, and He will speak with you.

entries.section: (1) The numbering of the people and the appointment of heads from the tribes

paragraphs.text: Their families: their tribes.
The house of their fathers: that is, the households.

By their armies: the divisions to which they belong according to the houses, the families and the tribes. The subject of the Lord's words to Moses was the command to number the people, "all the congregation," that is, to count the males able to go to war, whom God defined as those above twenty years of age. The Lord charged Moses and his brother Aaron to supervise the numbering themselves and under their direct responsibility, because of the importance of the matter.

This numbering is the first numbering of the children of Israel who came out of Egypt. There is another opinion, which is that Moses had made another numbering before the tabernacle of meeting was set up, and collected from the males the silver that went into the building of the tabernacle (Ex 38:25, 26).

entries.section: (1) The numbering of the people and the appointment of heads from the tribes

paragraphs.text: Because of the difficulty and importance of the work, God commanded Moses and Aaron to take the help of twelve men, who were the heads of the tribes, "each one head of the house of his fathers," to complete this counting. Here God teaches us two important things: the first is organization and prior planning for any work we undertake, and the other is an important principle, namely seeking the help of others and employing their abilities so that the work is accomplished more quickly and with the least weariness, as it also shows the role of the laity in the service of the Church.

entries.section: (1) The numbering of the people and the appointment of heads from the tribes

paragraphs.text: God mentioned to Moses and Aaron the names of the heads of the tribes and specified them, and the writing of their names here means that God is the One who chooses and calls, for He knows who is fit for this task. The mention of their names is also an honor and a lasting memorial to them and to their labors, for God does not forget anyone's labor. The indication here is also clear to us that whoever labors for the sake of Christ, His Church and His people will have his name written in the Book of Life in the Kingdom of Heaven. It is noticed that God mentioned first the name of the tribe and then the one responsible for numbering it, for we always belong to our spiritual fathers, as an extension of them and the fruit of their labor in us.
Elizur: its meaning is God is a rock, and he is head of the tribe of Reuben.
Shelumiel (v. 6): peace of God, and he is head of the tribe of Simeon.

Nahshon (v. 7): its meaning is serpent; he was the brother of Aaron's wife, is head of the tribe of Judah, and is mentioned in the genealogy of Christ (Mt 1:4). Nethaneel (v. 8): its meaning is God has given, and he is head of the tribe of Issachar.
Eliab (v. 9): God is Father, and he is head of the tribe of Zebulun.

The children of Joseph (v. 10): it is noticed that Joseph did not have a tribe of his own, although he was of the loins of Jacob, the father of all the tribes; but because God blessed Joseph with a blessing greater than all his brothers, he came to have two tribes in the persons of his sons (Manasseh and Ephraim). Elishama: God is my salvation, and he is head of the tribe of Ephraim.
Gamaliel: God repays the kindness (the reward), and he is head of the tribe of Manasseh.
Abidan (v. 11): my father is judge, and he is head of the tribe of Benjamin.
Ahiezer (v. 12): my brother is for help, and he is head of the tribe of Dan.
Pagiel (v. 13): God meets, and he is head of the tribe of Asher.
Eliasaph (v. 14): God has added to me, and he is head of the tribe of Gad.
Ahira (v. 15): its meaning is my brother is evil, and he is head of the tribe of Naphtali.

entries.section: (1) The numbering of the people and the appointment of heads from the tribes

paragraphs.text: After the choosing of the men, Moses the prophet declares to us their standing and the greatness of their rank among the people, making clear that they were in fact the most worthy of all to be chosen, for they were known to the whole people and were indeed the heads of the tribes and the source of their confidence, and they were also their judges, "heads of thousands"; for Moses had chosen for his people rulers of tens, rulers of fifties, rulers of hundreds and rulers of thousands to help him in governing and judging the people's troubles, in keeping with the counsel of his father-in-law Jethro, after he had been judging alone and it had wearied him greatly (Ex 18:21-23).

entries.section: (2) The actual numbering and the number of males in each tribe

paragraphs.text: The work began at once, as the Lord had said, for God's word to Moses had come on the first of the second month (v. 1), and here too the same time is mentioned for the beginning of the work. The work began with the whole congregation of the people gathering, divided by tribes; and since this numbering was only of the males able to go to war, these chosen heads recorded their names as the first of those numbered, so "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
By their polls: that is, this counting was exact and left out none of the males above twenty years of age.

Let us learn two things from this: the first is quickness in responding to God's word and His commandments and not postponing spiritual work, for quickness of response shows and brings out our love and obedience toward God; and the second is exactness and diligence in carrying out this work, for speed must not come at the expense of exactness, otherwise it would have no value.

entries.section: (2) The actual numbering and the number of males in each tribe

paragraphs.text: Their generations: that is, their births.
From twenty years old: that is, whoever was twenty years old, with no upper age limit so long as he was able to go to war.

The numbering began with the tribe of Reuben, who was indeed Jacob's firstborn in the flesh, even though the spiritual blessing went to Joseph because Reuben had angered his father (Gen 49:3, 4). The numbering of each tribe was recorded separately first. It is noticed in the numbering of each tribe:

(1) That it was approximate to the nearest hundred, so the numbers of tens or units were not mentioned in this numbering. (2) The emphasis on exactness, for the twelve heads of the tribes took part in it together with both "Moses" and "Aaron."

(3) The census states that the total number of all the males of the tribes reached 603,550 (v. 46), because if the units and tens were actually added up, this figure was rounded to the nearest ten. Statisticians in modern times say, according to population rates, that this means the number of the whole people was about two and a half million.

(4) The expression "all that were able to go forth to war" (v. 45) is an expression we ought to contemplate spiritually, for the spiritual life is a life of striving for the Lord and a war against Satan and the lusts of the world, and we have all come out of Baptism as spiritual soldiers counted in the army of God (2 Tim 2:3), and this war of ours continues throughout the days of our sojourn on earth. So do not be careless, my beloved brother, but trust in God's help to you, for God wants for you the victory and the crown, but you must want them too.

(5) This numbering also shows God's blessing upon the people, as His earlier promise to their great father Abraham (Gen 12:2), since their number when they entered Egypt with Jacob was 75 souls, and now, after their coming out of Egypt, their number had reached two and a half million.

(6) The Book of Exodus (Ex 12:37) mentions that the number of men who came out of Egypt after the ten plagues was six hundred thousand, while this census states that their number was six hundred thousand, three thousand, five hundred and fifty; the difference between the two numbers is the number of males who reached the age of twenty in the period of thirteen months from their coming out of Egypt to the beginning of the second month of the second year. (7) The census was useful in knowing the genealogies of the children of Israel, the importance of which appeared in knowing the genealogy of Christ.

entries.section: (3) The Levites were not numbered, and their duties

paragraphs.text: These verses show that, on the basis of God's command to Moses and His speaking with him (v. 1), the males of the tribe of Levi, that is, the Levites, were not counted or numbered, and their numbers were not included in the total of those going out to war, since God had prepared for them another work no less important than war itself, namely the service of the tabernacle of meeting.

entries.section: (3) The Levites were not numbered, and their duties

paragraphs.text: The tabernacle of the testimony: the tabernacle of meeting, which took this name because it contained within it the two tablets of the covenant, or the testimony, that is, the Ten Commandments.

Round about the tabernacle shall they encamp: the Levites used to dwell around the tabernacle of meeting on the north, west and south sides, while the priests dwelt on the east side before the door of the tabernacle (ch. 2). Here the task of the Levites becomes clear: it is to care for and guard the tabernacle of meeting and everything connected with it and all its inner contents, "the vessels thereof"; they alone are assigned to carry the tabernacle when traveling and journeying, and they perform the service inside it and outside it and dwell around it.

entries.section: (3) The Levites were not numbered, and their duties

paragraphs.text: They alone also have the right to take its parts apart when journeying and to set it up in the midst of the people when they settle. And everyone who is not of the tribe of Levi, that is, a stranger, is put to death, according to God's command, if he draws near, or touches, or lays a hand on the components or any part of the tabernacle.

entries.section: (3) The Levites were not numbered, and their duties

paragraphs.text: His camp: the place of his dwelling.
His standard: a flag or banner belonging to each tribe.
By their armies: that is, the tribe with its males counted for war.

When they settle and the tabernacle of meeting is set up, the people gather in order around the tabernacle, each tribe having its place and its flag, "its standard," and this will be discussed in detail in the second chapter.

entries.section: (3) The Levites were not numbered, and their duties

paragraphs.text: As for the tents of the Levites, they are to be the closest to the tabernacle of meeting and around it, and this is a second confirmation of what God had already mentioned in (v. 51), and it shows that their nearness to the tabernacle is because of their service to His house and their keeping the rites and ordinances of worship. And God charges all His people to carry out His word in this matter, or else the whole people would be exposed to wrath and punishment.

entries.section: (3) The Levites were not numbered, and their duties

paragraphs.text: The conclusion of this chapter comes to show that what the Lord commanded "Moses" in (v. 1) was carried out with the utmost exactness, fear and respect.

My beloved brother, have you seen with me how great was God's care for His house, that is, the tabernacle of meeting, and how He set apart for it a whole tribe, and how He kept strangers from drawing near it?! My brother, the tabernacle was a type of the Church of the New Testament, and with all it contained it did not reach the glory of the Church of God, which offers His Body and Blood. Do we then respect the house of God and revere it as is fitting? Be careful, beloved, and keep the words of the Lord Christ always in your ear, "The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up" (Jn 2:17), as you deal with His Church and its sacraments.
The tribes and their encampment around the tabernacle: introduction:

This chapter shows us that our God is a God of order and arrangement, and how He divided the twelve tribes into four groups, each group pitching its tents on one of the four sides of the tabernacle of meeting, and likewise God set an order for the journeying of the congregation when they travel.

entries.section: (1) The order and place of encampment of the tribes

paragraphs.text: His standard: a piece of cloth bearing some symbol or drawing or color.
Over against: in front of, or opposite.

The discourse was from God, the Supreme Commander of the march of His people, directed to the earthly leaders, that is, Moses and Aaron, and the subject of the discourse was how the tribes were to dwell around the tabernacle when it was set up .. and God's first command was that each group should have a flag that distinguishes it; and because each group consists of three tribes, the interpreters also saw that each tribe had another, smaller flag that distinguished it within the group. The flag of each tribe was distinct from the flags of the other tribes, and perhaps it bore what represents the prophecies of Jacob to his sons (Gen 49). The expression "round about it they shall encamp" is a beautiful expression showing God's concern that His people be around Him, while He is their God dwelling in their midst, caring for their every need.

We too have come to have a standard and a sign in the drawing of the holy Cross, by which we remember and call to mind the sufferings of our Redeemer the Lord Jesus and His love for us. Take care, my brother, to befriend this sign in all your works, for its power is exceedingly wonderful.

entries.section: (1) The order and place of encampment of the tribes

paragraphs.text: Camp: the place where the tents are pitched.

Camp of Dan, comprising the tribes of Dan, Asher and Naphtali. Merarites. Camp of Ephraim, comprising the tribes of north Ephraim, Manasseh and Benjamin. The outer court. Altar of burnt offering. Gershonites. The laver. East. West. Tabernacle of meeting. Moses and Aaron and his sons. Judah, Issachar and Zebulun. South. Camp of Judah, comprising the tribes. Kohathites. Camp of Reuben, comprising the tribes of Reuben, Simeon, Figure (1) The place of encampment of the tribes around the tabernacle. God began by fixing the place of the tents of the first group, which consists of three tribes, namely Judah, Issachar and Zebulun (Figure 1), and the following is noticed in this group:
1- Although they are three tribes, they were called "the camp of Judah," because he is the eldest and foremost among his brothers, and from him Christ will come.

2- This group occupied the eastern place, that is, in front of the main and only door of the tabernacle of meeting. And before it, on the side of the door, dwell Moses and Aaron and the rest of the priests. The camp of Judah was two thousand cubits from the tabernacle, that is, about one kilometer, and the farthest of its tents were about 1.5 km away, so that all the people were able to reach the tabernacle of meeting easily.

3- The names of the heads of the tribes are mentioned to show their standing and their authority in the organization; they are the same heads who helped Moses and Aaron in the counting and numbering of the people (ch. 1).

4- The number of males previously counted and ready for war is also mentioned, and after the number of the males of each tribe was given, they were all added together as the total of one group, namely "the camp of Judah," so the number of males of the eastern group reached one hundred and eighty-six thousand four hundred.

They shall first set forth: that is, they are the first people to take down their tents and lead the people on the march. It is noticed that in the tenth chapter too he will explain more fully the manner of the people's journeying and the order of the tribes in it.

entries.section: (1) The order and place of encampment of the tribes

paragraphs.text: The south: that is, the southern side.

God assigned the southern side for the encampment of three other tribes, namely the tribes of Reuben, Simeon and Gad, but the camp or group took the name of Reuben as the tribe placed at the head of the group, as happened with the group of Judah. Here too the males of each tribe were counted separately, and then the total of the whole group came to one hundred and fifty-one thousand four hundred and fifty, that is, the males numbered for war.
They shall set forth second: that is, when journeying they are the second group after the group of Judah.

entries.section: (2) The order of the journeying of the Levites and the rest of the tribes

paragraphs.text: After the groups of Judah and Reuben set forth, who are six tribes, that is, half the people, the tabernacle too is taken down and journeys in the midst of the people, that is, two groups, then the tabernacle, and after them two groups; and because the Levites alone have the right to carry the tabernacle with all its contents and vessels, their journeying is mentioned here as accompanying the journeying of the tabernacle.

Every man in his place by their standards: the Levites did not journey all at once but in companies, each company charged with carrying certain parts, and the order of the journeying of these companies comes as the tenth chapter will explain. These companies of the Levites were the "Gershonites," the "Merarites" and the "Kohathites," and each company among them had a flag or standard that distinguished it, and each of the three companies dwelt on a different side of the tabernacle, as the drawing at the end of the chapter shows.

entries.section: (2) The order of the journeying of the Levites and the rest of the tribes

paragraphs.text: As for the third group, it bore the name of Ephraim the son of Joseph and included, as usual, three tribes: with him were the tribe of Manasseh, the brother of Ephraim, and Benjamin. The names of the heads of the tribes and the number of those mustered for war for each tribe separately were also mentioned, and then the total of the three tribes together, and the total reached one hundred and eight thousand one hundred. Their order of journeying among the tribes was also the third.

entries.section: (2) The order of the journeying of the Levites and the rest of the tribes

paragraphs.text: Finally comes the fourth group, which was named "Dan" and also included the tribes of Asher and Naphtali, and the total of those reckoned in it for war was one hundred and fifty-seven thousand six hundred, and this fourth group was the last group in the journeying.
The following is noticed in the order of the encampment of the tribes:
1- God's concern for order and arrangement, so that this might be the way of His people in their lives and dealings.

2- Each of the four groups encamped around the tabernacle of meeting was of one kin: the group of Judah, encamped east of the tabernacle, included three of the sons of Leah, namely Judah, Issachar and Zebulun; the group of Reuben, encamped south of the tabernacle, included two of the sons of Leah, namely Reuben and Simeon, while Gad is the son of Zilpah, Leah's maid. The third group, encamped west of the tabernacle, is the group of Ephraim, which included Ephraim and Manasseh, the sons of Joseph, and Benjamin his brother, all of them of the offspring of Rachel. As for the fourth group, which encamps north of the tabernacle, it is the group of Dan and includes Dan and Naphtali, the sons of Bilhah, and Asher the son of Zilpah.

3- The tribe of Levi encamps around the tabernacle and close to it on three sides because they are charged with the service of the house of the Lord, while the priests encamp on the east side before the door of the tabernacle to perform their work in it.

4- It is noticed that the number of soldiers in the first group, which is the group of Judah that goes before the people when they set forth, includes the greatest number of soldiers, followed in number of soldiers by the fourth group, the group of Dan, which is in the rear, while the second and third groups are fewer in number and are in the middle, in order to protect the people, so that its front and its rear are strong to face the enemies.
5- The tabernacle of meeting is in the midst of the tribes of Israel, whether encamping or journeying, in order to guard it.

entries.section: (2) The order of the journeying of the Levites and the rest of the tribes

paragraphs.text: As a conclusion to what came in this chapter, the grand and final total of the whole number is mentioned, as it also came at the end of the first chapter (v. 46), including all the tribes or the four groups.

entries.section: (2) The order of the journeying of the Levites and the rest of the tribes

paragraphs.text: Moses the prophet makes clear here the Lord's command to him not to number the Levites with the people, since they had another service and became the portion of the Lord and servants of His house, although the third chapter will show us that there was also a numbering of the Levites that was their own, but we shall learn of it in its time.

entries.section: (2) The order of the journeying of the Levites and the rest of the tribes

paragraphs.text: And so the people kept the established order throughout nearly forty years, in their journeying and encamping, and they always carried their standards belonging to each group, each tribe and each family. We can draw some beneficial spiritual meanings from what came in this chapter:
1- God shows His love for us, for He wants to dwell in our midst as a tender Father, and for His children to gather around Him.
2- In His care for us, God set an order for His people in journeying and encamping, for order saves time and prevents confusion and children's getting lost among the great people.

3- The high standards were to guide anyone who strayed from his people during the journey: there was a standard for the group, another for the tribe and a smaller one for the family ... and this reminds us of the high lighthouse of the Church, guiding everyone who has strayed and wandered in the exile of the world.

4- We too must keep the commandments of the Lord during the journey of life, for it is easy for us also to wander in the world in which we live and lose our way to heaven. Let us fix our eyes on the Lord and His standard, which is His Cross, and keep our ears and hearts subject to all that He tells us, and deliverance will be written for us.

It is good that God be your leader in all your steps, so that you walk through life at peace, by lifting your prayers to Him before every work and by submitting to the guidance of the Church even if it differs from the thoughts of the world. The descendants of Moses and Aaron and the account of the Levites

entries.section: (1) The generations of Moses and Aaron

paragraphs.text: Generations: that is, descendants.

The name of Moses has always come before that of his brother Aaron, since he was the prophet of God and the one He spoke with. In this chapter, however, the name of Aaron comes first, for the following reasons:

1- All the discourse will be about the Levites and about matters relating to worship and to the priests who belong to Aaron. The sons of Moses did not share in the work of the priests, but were counted among the Levites of the clan of the Amramites, which belonged to the Kohathites.
2- Because the historical order requires that the name of Aaron and his sons be written first, since he is the elder brother of Moses.
3- It shows the humility of Moses, in that he did not exploit his position by mentioning his own name before his brother's, as long as the discourse was about the priesthood.

The expression "in the day that the Lord spake with Moses" takes us back to the same date on which the numbering began (ch. 1:1), which was the first day of the second month of the second year after the departure from Egypt.

entries.section: (1) The generations of Moses and Aaron

paragraphs.text: Filling their hands: their ordination and their offering of the sacrifices with their own hands before the Lord.
The priest's office: the ministry of the priesthood.

The sons of Aaron were four, and their names are given according to the order of their birth: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. Their names have been mentioned several times before in the books of Exodus and Leviticus. These four were chosen by God, and were consecrated and set apart for the holy ministry of the priesthood.

entries.section: (1) The generations of Moses and Aaron

paragraphs.text: The Holy Spirit-inspired text returns to what was already mentioned in the Book of Leviticus (ch. 10:1, 2), because of the awesomeness of this event and to remind everyone of it: when the glory of the Lord came down upon the Tabernacle while Moses and Aaron were inside it, fire came down from God and consumed the holy burnt offering and kindled the altar. This divine fire became the source of every fire used in worship thereafter. The sin of Nadab and Abihu was that they did not use this divine fire, but used common fire which they brought in from outside, in carelessness and indifference toward the order that God had established. Therefore God's punishment was a deterrent: a divine fire came out from within the Tabernacle and consumed them at once. When they died they had no offspring to inherit the ministry after them, and so of the sons of Aaron only Eleazar and Ithamar remained, serving with their father before the Lord.

The Lord our God is long-suffering and patient with sinners, but He is also jealous for His Church and for the spirit of worship in it. So beware, beloved, of carelessness in dealing with God and His rights, and do not rely on God's mercies where they do not apply. Do not forget that the Lord Christ Himself, though He loves sinners and forgives adulterers, is also the One who rebuked the priests, the scribes and the Pharisees, and drove the sellers out of His house with the utmost firmness.

entries.section: (2) The calling of the Levites to serve the house

paragraphs.text: Bring the tribe of Levi near: set apart and consecrate the Levites.
Before Aaron: preparing them to take part in the work with him.
That they may minister unto him: Aaron is to have the authority of organizing the worship.

The Lord commanded Moses to bring the males of the Levites, since God had chosen them and set them apart for the service of the Tabernacle, and declared that they would work under the leadership of Aaron the priest to help him in the ministry, with the tasks that would be entrusted to them afterward. The Levites here resemble the ministry of the deacons in the Church, who help the priests in the congregational worship and its arrangements, and who serve under their authority.

Here the mercies of God toward the tribe of Levi appear, whose father sinned in the incident at Shechem (Gen 34:25, 26). Yet through his repentance God turned his descendants to service, so that they became consecrated to God, and from them came the priesthood that leads the people in worship. Moreover, the Levites became a redemption and a substitute for the firstborn of the children of Israel (ch. 8). The Levites' adherence to the worship of God and their faith in Him appeared in the incident of the golden calf (Ex 32), when they obeyed Moses and slew those who insisted on worshiping the calf.

entries.section: (2) The calling of the Levites to serve the house

paragraphs.text: His charge: that is, the commands and directions of Aaron.
The charge of the whole congregation: that is, carrying out the ritual order for all the people.
The tabernacle: a word God used to describe the tent of meeting, as the dwelling in which He dwells in the midst of His people.

The first task that God appointed to the Levites was to receive the arrangements and rites of worship from Aaron with all precision and care, because they are also responsible before God for teaching these things and handing them on to the people and the whole congregation. The expression "to do the service of the tabernacle" is an introduction to the coming verses, in which God will explain some matters of this service.

entries.section: (2) The calling of the Levites to serve the house

paragraphs.text: The charge of the children of Israel: that is, they act on behalf of all the people in keeping the house of God.

The clans of the Levites, in their dwelling places, surrounded the Tabernacle, that is, they were between the Tabernacle and the tribes. Their first task was therefore to guard the Tabernacle, outwardly as a building, so that no one would approach it, and inwardly, all its contents, that is, its furnishings. This confirms that they alone were responsible for the service of the tabernacle.

entries.section: (2) The calling of the Levites to serve the house

paragraphs.text: The whole tribe of Levi is regarded as an offering from all the people to God, that is, a response to God's love and care. The children of Israel offered one tribe from among them to be consecrated to the service of God and His tabernacle, and they offered it to God by presenting it to Aaron, the leader of the priesthood, who then distributed them among the various services as the Lord commanded.

entries.section: (2) The calling of the Levites to serve the house

paragraphs.text: You shall appoint: you shall establish and assign work to him.
The stranger: any person who is not of the offspring of Aaron and the Levites, even if he is one of the people of God.
Aaron and his sons were to keep their priesthood. The meaning here is to carry out the priestly ministry and to preserve it and be zealous for it against the interference of any outsider.

God's warning was fearful to all the people: no one may approach this holy service except the priests of the house of Aaron, and whoever tries to encroach upon it or approach it shall be punished with death, as God Himself did with Korah and his brethren when they tried to offer incense to the Lord though they were not priests (this incident will be discussed in detail in ch. 16), and as He destroyed Uzzah, who touched the ark of the covenant of God (2 Sam 6:6, 7). Jewish tradition adds that the Jews afterward hung a golden sword on the outer door of the Tabernacle as a sign and reminder of this divine command that anyone who touches or deals with the Tabernacle and its holy things, other than the priests and the Levites, shall die.

My beloved brother ... perhaps you or one of the members of your family has received one of the ranks of the diaconate and has been called to serve the house of the Lord. Do not neglect this great service, then, and encourage your children also to commit themselves to it. There is nothing better than that God should set us apart as deacons to preserve order and worship in His house, for it is a great and honorable responsibility that the deacons, together with the priests, preserve the inheritance, the tradition and the rites of the Church.

entries.section: (3) The Levites as the redemption of the firstborn of the people

paragraphs.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses: this expression means the continuation of the previous discourse, but it is an introduction to opening a new subject within the same discourse.

entries.section: (3) The Levites as the redemption of the firstborn of the people

paragraphs.text: Here God, in His humility, explains to the people His wisdom in choosing the Levites for Himself and for His service. He takes the people's memory back to the time He smote the firstborn of the Egyptians, both of men and of beasts (Ex 12), and how God afterward commanded that all the firstborn of the people, of men and of beasts as well, be set apart for Him, since every one that opens the womb was a portion set apart for the Lord (Ex 13 ...). If the firstborn was an animal, it was offered as a sacrifice to God, but if it was a human being, five shekels of silver were offered in his place.

Here, however, after the building of the Tabernacle, God makes clear that the Levites became instead of the firstborn of the people. The words "the Levites shall be mine" are a new clarification of the special position of this tribe, of its belonging to God and of its service to Him.

Let us examine our hearts every day: are they truly consecrated to God and the dwelling place of His Holy Spirit? ... God set us apart for Himself and anointed our hearts with the oil of the Holy Myron when we received the sacrament of Baptism. But we must preserve this seal and this consecration, and remember that when God chose our hearts for His dwelling, they became His dwelling and His house alone, and it is not fitting for any stranger or foreigner, that is, any sin or lust, to dwell in it or come near it.

entries.section: (4) The account of the clans of the Levites

paragraphs.text: After the numbering of the males of the people able to go to war from all the tribes (ch. 1), the Lord gave Moses a new charge, which was to number the males of the Levites, but from the age of one month and not from the age of 20 years, as for those who went out to war. This is because the men of the tribe of Levi who would serve God must be prepared from their childhood to be God's.

The Levites began their work from the age of 25 years until fifty (ch. 8:24, 25). God sanctified many of His prophets and saints in their earliest childhood: He called Jeremiah while he was in his mother's womb (Jer 1:5), and John the Baptist was also filled with the Spirit in his mother's womb, and the Church gives children entry into the first ranks of the diaconate, which is the Epsaltos, that is, the chanter.

This reminds us to care for our children from their childhood and to bind them to the Church, especially since she teaches us this through the sacrament of Baptism, which takes place at the beginning of their lives, and she commands us to give them spiritual care through partaking of the Holy Mysteries and through their attachment to the Church's schools of education.

entries.section: (4) The account of the clans of the Levites

paragraphs.text: Moses numbered the Levites as God commanded, mentioning the heads of their fathers' houses. It is noted that the heads of the clans of the Levites were three great men, sons of Levi the son of Jacob, and from these three came all the clans of the Levites. These three are mentioned in the order of their ages: "Gershon," the father of all the Gershonites; "Kohath," the origin of the clans of the Kohathites, who are the origin of Moses and Aaron; and the third is "Merari," from whom came all the tribes and clans of the Merarites.

entries.section: (4) The account of the clans of the Levites

paragraphs.text: After mentioning the sons of Levi, it mentions here the grandsons, who were eight, each of whom afterward founded a clan that bore his name. The two sons of Gershon were "Libni" and "Shimei," heads of their clans. The sons of Kohath were "Amram," "Izhar," "Hebron" and "Uzziel," and they became the heads of their clans. And the two sons of Merari were "Mahli" and "Mushi," likewise heads of their clans.

May we care about bringing up our children, because the traits of a person's character are formed in his early childhood. Caring for them is the most important work we offer them throughout their lives, and tenderness with guidance and sharing in their play is what forms in them a sound, stable and successful personality throughout life.

entries.section: (5) The distribution of responsibilities among the clans of the Levites after they were numbered

paragraphs.text: As stated in (v. 18), Moses reminds us again that the clans of the "Libnites and the Shimites" belong to their father Gershon, and their number at the numbering was seven thousand five hundred males, from a month old and upward.

entries.section: (5) The distribution of responsibilities among the clans of the Levites after they were numbered

paragraphs.text: Just as God set for the tribes places and standards around the tent of meeting, here He fixes the place of the clans of the Gershonites, that their tents be on the west of the Tabernacle, that is, opposite the Holy of Holies (see the illustration at the end of the chapter). To organize their dwelling and work and to settle problems, "Eliasaph the son of Lael" was chosen as chief over all the Gershonites, that is, over both families together.

entries.section: (5) The distribution of responsibilities among the clans of the Levites after they were numbered

paragraphs.text: The work with which the two clans of the Gershonites were charged was the care of the Tabernacle, taking it apart and carrying it when journeying, and then putting it together again, that is, setting it up when encamping. The detail of their responsibility and charge was as follows:

1- The tabernacle: the structure of the Tent, made of boards, pillars and bars, which formed its frame, and likewise the cloth curtains, which formed its walls, with their various beautiful colors (see Ex 26). The Gershonites were assigned to carry the cloth but not the wood of the tabernacle, since the wood was the portion of the "Merarites," as will come in (v. 36).
2- The tent: the outer covering of the Tent, which was of goats' hair.
3- The covering: this includes a covering of rams' skins and another of badgers' skins (a sea animal).
4- The hanging for the door: the screen over the door of the tent of meeting, which was set up on five pillars.
5- The hangings of the court: the linen curtains that surround the courtyard of the Tent and are hung on wooden pillars, so they were a wall for the Tent.
6- The hanging for the door of the court: the screen that was on the door of the outer court on the east side.
7- Its cords: the ropes used to fasten the parts of the Tent to one another and also used to stretch it to the pins.
8- That which is around the tabernacle and around the altar: that is, the curtains that form the outer boundary, and likewise the inner curtains that divide the Tent into parts.

9- All the service thereof: that is, all the other matters connected with the foregoing are in the charge of the Gershonites. (See the pictures of the Tabernacle and its contents in the second volume of the Encyclopedia of the Interpretation of the Old Testament, that is, the books of Exodus and Leviticus.)

entries.section: (5) The distribution of responsibilities among the clans of the Levites after they were numbered

paragraphs.text: The second group of the Levites, after the Gershonites, are the Kohathites, and the details of their clans are also given here for the second time: the Amramites (Amram is the father of Moses, Aaron and Miriam), the Izharites, the Hebronites, and finally the clan of the Uzzielites. The total number of males in these clans, from a month old, was eight thousand six hundred, and their task and responsibility was to keep the sanctuary and the Holy of Holies and their contents and to watch over them. The details will come in (v. 31).

entries.section: (5) The distribution of responsibilities among the clans of the Levites after they were numbered

paragraphs.text: As God did before in fixing the place of the Gershonites, so He does here also, and fixes the south of the Tabernacle as the place for the Kohathites, where they pitch their tents. He also chose a chief over all the clans of the Kohathites, "Elizaphan the son of Uzziel."

entries.section: (5) The distribution of responsibilities among the clans of the Levites after they were numbered

paragraphs.text: This verse gives the detail of the contents of the sanctuary and the Holy of Holies, to make clear the duties of the Kohathites.

1- The ark: they carried it without touching it, by means of two staves, and they did not look at it, since the priests covered it before it was carried. It afterward contained the tables of the covenant, that is, the tables of the Law, and the rod of Aaron the priest, and the pot of manna. After the Tabernacle was set up, the place of the ark was in the Holy of Holies.
2- The table: the table of the showbread (Ex 25:23), on which twelve loaves were placed, and its place was in the sanctuary. The priests also covered it before it was carried.
3- The golden lampstand: see its description in (Ex 25:31). It too was covered, like those before it, before it was carried.

4- The altars: these are the altar of burnt offering in the outer court and the golden altar of incense inside the sanctuary. The details of each altar and its use were already explained in the Book of Exodus.
5- The vessels of the sanctuary: the small vessels and tools with which they minister, such as tongs and censers and other tools, or things larger in size, such as the laver.
6- The veil and all the service thereof: that is, a summary of all the foregoing, meaning everything that is behind the veil and is used in the ritual service.

My beloved brother, our Church took over many of the arrangements that God Himself established for dividing the work between the priests and the deacons, as was the case anciently between the priests and the Levites. So preparing and arranging the tools of the altar became the responsibility of the deacons, but as for the holy vessels themselves, the deacon has no right to touch them with the bare hand, but only with wrappings, to hallow them and to honor their worth ... If the things of old in the Tabernacle had this dignity, how much more the vessels of the altar of the covenant of grace and redemption.

entries.section: (5) The distribution of responsibilities among the clans of the Levites after they were numbered

paragraphs.text: Chief over the chief of the Levites, with the oversight of them that keep the charge of the sanctuary: that is, the headship over all the chiefs of the Levites in what relates to the ritual work and worship.
Before God, Eleazar the son of Aaron was responsible for leading the work of the Levites, supervising their chiefs in the performance of their ministry and all their works.

entries.section: (5) The distribution of responsibilities among the clans of the Levites after they were numbered

paragraphs.text: The third group is the group of the "Merarites," which has the two clans of "the Mahlites and the Mushites." As was the case with the two previous groups ... the number of their males in the census is also mentioned here, which came to six thousand two hundred, and their chief is also mentioned, Zuriel the son of Abihail. As for the place of the clans of the Merarites, it was toward the north, as shown in the drawing at the end of the chapter.

entries.section: (5) The distribution of responsibilities among the clans of the Levites after they were numbered

paragraphs.text: As for their work and the responsibility with which God charged them, it was as follows:

1- The boards of the tabernacle and its bars: the boards of the tabernacle are wooden boards made of acacia wood and overlaid with gold, and they formed the inner walls of the Tent (see Ex 26:15-29). The bars were the supports that fixed the boards and joined them to one another.
2- Its sockets: the bases of the pillars, made of silver.
3- All the vessels thereof and all the service thereof: that is, everything connected with the boards and the bars.
4- The pillars of the court round about: that is, the wooden pillars of the outer court of the Tent, that is, the enclosure.

5- Their sockets, and their pins, and their cords: their sockets, that is, the silver bases; and the pins are the wooden pieces that fix the pillars in the ground, inside and outside the Tent, and to which the pillars are drawn by the ropes, that is, the cords.
It is noted that the charge of the Merarites was the heaviest of the things in the Tent, and carrying it when journeying.

entries.section: (5) The distribution of responsibilities among the clans of the Levites after they were numbered

paragraphs.text: As for the last side, the east side, which is in front of the entrance of the door of the Tent, God assigned it to Moses the prophet and his brother Aaron the priest and their offspring. In origin Moses and Aaron are Levites of the group of the Kohathites, the clan of the Amramites, but they took a separate place, since Aaron came to represent the priesthood with his sons and Moses is the prophet of God. The responsibility that God entrusted to them with their sons was:

1- Keeping the charge of the sanctuary: that is, the general and comprehensive care of the Tent and all that it contains and of the worship, and supervision of all the groups of the Levites. The expression "keeping the charge of the sanctuary" implicitly includes offering the sacrifices.
2- For the charge of the children of Israel: that is, they act on behalf of all the people of Israel in preserving the holy things connected with the Tent.

3- The stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death: the stranger here includes not only those foreign to the people but also anyone who is an outsider with no connection to the priesthood, even if he is of the people themselves. For in order to show His jealousy for His house, God forbade any person to enter and tamper with the holy things of the house, and so that the punishment might be a deterrent, He made it death.

entries.section: (5) The distribution of responsibilities among the clans of the Levites after they were numbered

paragraphs.text: This verse mentions the total number of the Levites in their three groups, which is twenty-two thousand ... whereas if we add these groups together we find them to be twenty-two thousand three hundred. It is said that the difference of three hundred were the firstborn of the Levites themselves, whom their fathers had redeemed first, together with all the firstborn of the tribes (Ex 13), before the numbering of the tribes, and for this reason they were excluded from the count here.

Let there be a definite ministry, even a small one, that you offer to God. For merely carrying the parts of the Tent was a great matter, so how much greater it will be if you offer a ministry to the Church, and the greatest ministry is to bring a person who is far away into her embrace.

entries.section: (6) The Levites as a substitute for the firstborn of the people

paragraphs.text: The first numbering (ch. 1) was of the males of the people able to go to war, above the age of twenty years. The numbering that the Lord commanded Moses in this verse is like the numbering of the Levites, that is, from a month old and upward. This numbering was of the firstborn males only (v. 42), and He commanded him to write down this numbering of the males of the tribes, by numbers and names, for the sake of accuracy.

entries.section: (6) The Levites as a substitute for the firstborn of the people

paragraphs.text: The purpose of this numbering was to substitute the firstborn of the Levites for the firstborn of all the people. To understand this point we shall explain it in detail ...

After the Lord slew the firstborn of the Egyptians, both of men and of beasts (Ex 12:29; Ex 13:1-2), He commanded the people that every firstborn be offered as a portion to the Lord, whether of the people's sons or of their beasts. By this new numbering God wished to relieve the people from offering their firstborn, and to set apart the firstborn of the Levites in place of the firstborn of the people.

And just as the men of the tribe of Levi were counted instead of the firstborn of the children of Israel, so too their beasts were all set apart for God instead of the firstborn of the beasts of the children of Israel.

entries.section: (6) The Levites as a substitute for the firstborn of the people

paragraphs.text: When "Moses" finished numbering the firstborn by their names, their number was 22,273 (twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three), that is, an excess of two hundred and seventy-three (273) over the number of the men of the Levites.

entries.section: (6) The Levites as a substitute for the firstborn of the people

paragraphs.text: The numbers were very close, so the Lord commanded Moses to substitute the men of the tribe of Levi for the firstborn of the people, as a redemption for them, and likewise the beasts of the Levites for the firstborn of the beasts of the people, so that the Levites as a whole, and what they possess, become a portion for the Lord.
I am the Lord: a parenthetical expression whose purpose is to affirm that this command and this order have God alone as their source.

What an honor it is that God ascribes His own to His holy name. It is a glory that has been granted to us, since after Baptism we have all become His, bearing His seal. But, beloved, do you truly feel that your soul is consecrated to God and that everything you own is His? If you have not thought this way before, then remember from today that you are wholly God's, and that what you own is a gift from Him, so that you may manage it faithfully as His steward.

entries.section: (6) The Levites as a substitute for the firstborn of the people

paragraphs.text: Shekel: it is considered the first weighed silver coin known to the people, and is estimated at about fifteen grams.
Gerah: this is 1/20 of the shekel, that is, the shekel equals 20 gerahs.

The shekel of the sanctuary: that is, the shekel exact in its weight (the standard). As for the surplus of the firstborn of the people who have no counterpart among the firstborn of the Levites, whose number is two hundred and seventy-three, their redemption is as follows:

Five silver shekels of exact weight are to be paid for each male, like the shekels kept with the priests, which represent the true weight, and it is mentioned that each shekel equals 20 gerahs, to confirm the weight and the value required. A question may arise here for some: on what basis were the two hundred and seventy-three who owed the silver ransom determined?

Although there are many opinions, the closest to reality is that the choice was made by one of the methods of casting lots with which all were satisfied, as a system that avoids partiality in choosing.

entries.section: (6) The Levites as a substitute for the firstborn of the people

paragraphs.text: The total silver collected as a substitute and redemption for the firstborn of the people in excess of the Levites amounted to one thousand three hundred and sixty-five shekels, by the fixed weight, that is, the shekel of the sanctuary. Moses gave the silver that he had collected to Aaron and his sons the priests, as the Lord commanded, since they alone are responsible for the ministry and its needs.
The distribution of the service among the clans of the Levites when journeying

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: The Lord spoke: an expression common throughout the book, meaning that God is the source of the command and direction. The command here is to number the sons of Kohath with all their clans. It is known that Kohath was the second son of Levi and not the firstborn, but the Kohathites come first here because of the greatness of the tasks with which they will be charged, which include the inner implements of worship, as we shall see (v. 4).

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: This numbering is new. After God charged Moses to number all the males from a month old, to be taken as a ransom for the firstborn of all the people (ch. 3), He asks him here for a new numbering, of the males from thirty years old to fifty, which is the age period in which a man is able to exert himself in work and to endure hardships.

Although the eighth chapter of this book (ch. 8:24) states that the age of enlistment for the service of the house of the Lord among the Levites is 25 years, the meaning is that from the age of 25 to 30 years is a period of training and of sharing in the lesser services. It is noted that in the days of David and Ezra (1 Chr 23:24-32; Ezra 3:8) enlistment was at the age of twenty, that is, there was a training period of ten years until they reached the age of thirty. John the Baptist and also Christ began their ministries at the age of thirty.

Although enlistment for war in the other tribes begins at the age of twenty (ch. 1:3), we find that enlistment for the service of the house of the Lord in the tribe of Levi begins at the age of thirty, because of the greatness and importance of the service of the house of the Lord above any other work.

All that enter into the host: God regarded what He would charge them with as exactly like enlistment, for the work in the tent of meeting is an awesome task that requires devotion and concentration. Indeed, the service of God in general requires the spirit of the fighting soldier, as St. Paul enjoined his disciple Timothy when he said to him, "Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ" (2 Tim 2:3).

My beloved brother, God in His love has called us to the service of His holy name, and because of the greatness of this calling He warns us to be soldiers in His service, watchful on guard. He does not accept the negligent or the slack, but curses him. So if you are a servant in the Church of God, be strong, look to the reward, and be watchful lest anyone take your crown.

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: God assigned the service of the Kohathites to the Holy of Holies, which is similar in its holiness to the sanctuary and the altar in the Church. It is the place where God was manifested when He appeared in His glory, and the ark of the covenant was placed in it. In fact, the service of the Kohathites included two places, "the sanctuary" and "the Holy of Holies," and everything they contain.

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: When the camp is to set forward: that is, when the divine command to depart or move was issued, and this command came by the pillar of cloud being lifted up from above the Tabernacle (Ex 40:36). When preparing to depart, Aaron and his sons, who are the priests and the only ones permitted to touch the holy things and the implements with their hands, began by taking down the veil that separated the sanctuary from the Holy of Holies, and covered the ark of the covenant with it.

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: As a second covering over the veil in which the ark was wrapped, they put the skin of a thick sea animal (badger), and then they bring a final outer covering, a cloth of sky-blue. It is noted that the ark and the table alone were covered with three coverings, while the rest of the implements would be covered with only two. "And shall put in the staves thereof": the staves by which the ark was carried were always kept in the side rings. This expression means that the covering also includes the staves, so that the Levites would not carry them with bare hands.

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: The table of showbread: the table placed in the sanctuary, on which twelve loaves are placed, representing the constant presence of the tribes before the face of God.
Bowls: small vessels.

The way of covering the table before carrying it was as follows: first a cloth of blue ("hyacinth") is spread directly on the table, and over it is placed the bread, which must always be present before God, even when departing and journeying. The same applies to the implements used around the table, of dishes, bowls and cups.

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: The second covering comes over it, a cloth of scarlet, that is, red, the color of blood, and then the third covering over all of that, the thick skin that insulates, providing the highest degree of protection for the holy things by isolating them completely from dust. Symbolically, one may meditate on these coverings as follows ... The first, the sky-blue, points to Christ who comes from heaven to become incarnate, and who covered the twelve Apostles (the bread) with His glory. After that came the covering of the shed blood, which gives forgiveness and salvation, while the covering of thick skin points to the life of strictness in which the believer must live and by which he separates himself from evil.

And they put the staves in the rings of the table, which protrude outside the coverings, so that they may carry it by them. The Holy Bible says "the staves thereof," and it means the staves of the table of the showbread that was on the table.

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: The bar: two rods on which cross pieces of wood are fixed, to carry on it the lampstand or the other implements of the Tent.

As for the lampstand with seven lamps, whose place was in the sanctuary, it was covered with all its accessories and implements, the tongs and the oil vessels, first with a sky-blue covering and after that with an outer covering of the thick badger skin.

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: The golden altar: the inner altar of incense.
It too is covered with a blue cloth and then a covering of the skin of the thick badger animal.

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: As for the rest of the implements of the service that were not mentioned, such as the priests' garments or any other belongings, they are placed in the sky-blue cloth and also covered with the thick skin like the foregoing, and after this they are put on the carrier (the bar).

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: As for the outer altar of burnt offering, which is the bronze altar and whose place is at the entrance of the Tent, before covering it they had to remove the ashes left from the previous sacrifices and throw them in a place called "the place of the ashes," while the holy fire of the altar was carried in a special vessel throughout their journey. After the ashes and the holy fire were removed, they covered it with all its vessels needed for the service with a cloth of purple (royal red), since this altar, the altar of burnt offering, is a type of Christ the crucified King. Then comes after this the insulating covering of badger skin, and after covering the bronze altar they put its two staves in the rings and carried it by these staves.
The implements of the altar that are mentioned were:

The censers: the vessels in which burning coals are carried and which are used in burning incense, like the censer. The fleshhooks: a fork with three teeth and a long handle, used to take up or arrange the pieces of meat on the altar.
The shovels: the scoop used to shovel the ashes or to redistribute them on the altar.
The basins: vessels like bowls, used to collect the blood of the sacrifices so as to sprinkle it or throw it again as the matters of worship require.

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: The setting forward of the camp: the setting forward of the congregation of the children of Israel.

After the role of the priests, that is, Aaron and his sons, in wrapping and covering everything that was in the sanctuary and the Holy of Holies is finished, the role of the Levites comes, among them the sons of Kohath, and they carry these things without touching with their hands anything under these coverings, otherwise they would die. This is a strong warning from God to them, which makes them exceedingly careful in carrying and moving, and keeps far from them any suspicion of making light of these holy things.

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: Eleazar the son of Aaron had been appointed before this as general overseer of all the clans of the Levites in their work when setting forward or encamping (ch. 3:32), but here He makes clear other matters that were to be under his direct charge, which are:
- The oil for the light: the oil used to light the lamps of the lampstand.

- The sweet incense: the incense offered daily, morning and evening, on the altar of incense. - The daily meat offering: which is also the daily offering morning and evening (see Exodus 30:22-32). - The oversight of all the tabernacle: that is, no responsibility is excepted from Eleazar the priest, for everything is done under his personal and direct supervision.

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: God begins a new discourse with Moses and Aaron, laying on them a new responsibility, which is that the clans of the Kohathites not be cut off from the tribe of the Levites.

The meaning is that Aaron and his sons the priests must continually supervise, caution and warn the Kohathites, lest they touch any of the vessels or holy things with their hands and die and be cut off, and the negligence of Aaron and his sons the priests would be the cause of that, that is, the indirect cause of the destruction of the Kohathites.

How grave is the responsibility of the priests, since God has set them in the place of shepherds over His sheep, and He charges them with care and shepherding lest any of His flock perish, and Christ will require the blood of the sheep at the hand of the priest. If the responsibility is so great and fearful ... then, my brother, will you accept teaching or warning or even rebuke, if God allows it from the mouth of the priest ... If only you would do so, then you will not be cut off nor perish from before the Lord.

entries.section: (1) The service of the sons of Kohath

paragraphs.text: This warning came as a confirmation and completion of what was said before: no clan of the clans of the Levites is allowed to enter the sanctuary or the Holy of Holies lest they die, for no one enters these two places except the priests alone, and the punishment is plain and explicit if anything contrary to this happens.

entries.section: (2) The service of the Gershonites

paragraphs.text: These three verses correspond exactly to verses (1-3) at the beginning of the chapter. As He said at the choosing of the Kohathites, He says here at the choosing of the Gershonites, as an introduction to the service that will be assigned to them.

entries.section: (2) The service of the Gershonites

paragraphs.text: The service and the burden: the service means the care of the things, while the burden is a reference to carrying them during moving and journeying. The service of the Gershonites can be set out in detail as follows:-

1- The curtains of the tabernacle: that is, the coverings of the Tent from above and from the sides. They were made of the finest linen fabrics, and their colors were blue, purple and scarlet, a reference to the blue sky, the garments of the King, and the blood of the Redeemer.
2- The tent of the congregation: that is, the outer coverings made of goats' hair.
3- The outer covering: which was made of the skin of the sea animal, the badger.
4- The hanging for the door of the tent of the congregation: the door on the east side, which was also of fine cloth.

entries.section: (2) The service of the Gershonites

paragraphs.text: After the previous verse spoke about carrying the inner things, this verse moves us to speak about carrying the parts of the outer court that surrounds the tent of meeting.
1- The hangings of the court: those made of linen, five cubits high (see Ex 26:9-10).

2- The hanging for the gate of the court: the outer door of the outer court, also on the east side, and its height is like the height of the hangings, that is, five cubits, and its breadth 20 cubits (Ex 27:16). The hangings of the outer court were like the wall that surrounds the Tent and the altar of burnt offering.
3- The cords: the ropes that tied the various coverings of the Tent at departure, and any ropes used inside the Tent.

4- All the instruments of their service: that is, all the other tools connected with the inner curtains or the outer coverings, and anything the service needs or that may be damaged, which no one makes except the Gershonites.

entries.section: (2) The service of the Gershonites

paragraphs.text: All the work of the Gershonites is done under the supervision of the high priest Aaron and his sons the priests as well, and they are entrusted with watchfulness and care, that is, guarding everything God entrusted to them, and their direct chief in the supervision is the priest Ithamar the son of Aaron.

Covering precious things preserves them ... If only you would not speak much without need, and would keep the word of God within you and think on it so as to apply it in your life, and would persuade people of the truth more than much speaking that has no effect.

entries.section: (3) The service of the Merarites

paragraphs.text: As came by way of an introduction to the service of the previous groups.

entries.section: (3) The service of the Merarites

paragraphs.text: The service of the Merarites was the heavy things, such as:
1- The boards of the tabernacle (Ex 26:15-25:), which are the wooden boards overlaid with plates of gold and are regarded as the walls of the Tent.
2- The bars of the tabernacle: wood also overlaid with gold, which binds the boards to one another by means of rings of gold (Ex 26:26-29).

3- Its pillars and its sockets: that is, the pillars on which the veil and the hangings are hung, that is, the inner curtains that serve as doors for the sanctuary, the Holy of Holies and the outer door of the Tent; and the sockets are the silver bases on which the pillars are fixed (Ex 26:31, 32, 36, 37).

entries.section: (3) The service of the Merarites

paragraphs.text: The discourse here is about the outer court and its furnishings:
1- The pillars of the court round about: that is, the outer wooden pillars, and this also includes the silver rods that bind the pillars to one another.
2- Their sockets: the bases on which the pillars of the enclosure stand, but here they are of bronze and not silver.
3- The pins: which are of bronze and were around the outer court.
4- The cords: the ropes belonging to the outer court, for tying them to the outer bronze pins to hold them fast.

5- Their instruments and all their service: that is, all the equipment, contents, appurtenances and accessories. God commanded that lists be prepared defining the responsibility of each Levite in what he carries: "by name ye shall reckon the instruments," as a charge that he receives and hands over and watches over throughout the period of carrying so that nothing of it is lost.

My beloved brother, notice with me God's care for the implements of the service and how He regards them as a personal charge for which the Levite is held accountable ... How much more, then, is the charge of the souls entrusted to the bishop, the priest or the servant, which is far more precious, since their loss cannot be made good ... Have mercy on us, O Lord, and help us to serve all the souls in need, and complete the weakness of the work of Your servants ... Amen.

entries.section: (3) The service of the Merarites

paragraphs.text: Likewise the priest Ithamar is responsible for them and supervises them, as he is also chief over the Gershonites.

entries.section: (1) The separation of persons and the unclean

paragraphs.text: Leper: leprosy is a skin disease that people have differed in describing. It is either a disease resembling the skin disease psoriasis, which appears in the form of scaly patches on the skin ... or it may resemble the skin disease vitiligo, in which the color of the skin turns snow white, or it may be a skin disease that affects the nerves and causes pain ... Some see that the "leprosy" mentioned in the Old Testament was a general name embracing all the foregoing skin diseases and perhaps others as well. The word leprosy means in Hebrew (calamity), to indicate the severity and gravity of this disease, especially in its spiritual meaning, as we shall see. An issue: the discourse on issues of their various kinds came in the Book of Leviticus, such as the bodily discharges of a man and a woman, in which the person, the clothes and the bed are considered in a state of uncleanness requiring cleansing, if the matter was occasional, like a nocturnal emission or the monthly period; but if the matter was chronic or continuous, then the separation is outside the camp, which is the place where the people dwell (see Lev 15). Defiled by the dead: that is, everyone who touched a dead person or entered a tent in which there was a dead person ... The discourse about that came in the Book of Leviticus in many places, and it will also be mentioned in the Book of Numbers in the two chapters (12, 19). The speech of God to Moses was decisive, that he should separate every leper, or one with a continuing issue, or one defiled by the dead, to make clear an important meaning for the people ... for the holy God, who dwells in the midst of His people, never accepts sin in His presence, and because leprosy, the issue and death are either divine strokes resulting from sin, like leprosy in particular, or a sickness arising from sin, like the issue, and death is the wages of sin ... all these souls are separated in tents of their own outside the camp, for there is no fellowship of light with darkness. We note in this the following:

1- In God's mercies they were not left in the wilderness to die, but were separated in a place of their own for the sake of repentance. So also the Church may separate (excommunicate) some of her children from Communion or from attending church because of their corruption and their refusal to repent, but she does not cast them away; rather she cares for them outside until they return healthy, as she separated the sinner of Corinth and then received him after his repentance (1 Cor 5:1-5; 2 Cor 2:5-11).

2- The idea of separation also has two other purposes: preventing the spread of infection (the stumbling block) among the members of the camp (the Church), and likewise the decisive punishment is a deterrent to a person when he sees with his own eyes the result of sin, so that he avoids it.

Thus the Church has always been decisive in separating those who cause stumbling and in excommunicating heretics. The heretic who brings teachings foreign to the faith is more deadly and dangerous to the flock than the leper or the one with an issue, for he pollutes minds with his thoughts and ruins the faith of the Church which she received through time from her Christ and His pure Apostles ... So, beloved, let no pity take you for one who ruins souls, and remember the saying and warning of the Apostle, "Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person."

entries.section: (1) The separation of persons and the unclean

paragraphs.text: The punishment does not distinguish between man and woman, for sin is one for all, and there is no partiality or sparing of one sex over the other ... Everyone who sins or whom God smites with sickness as a result of sin is separated outside the congregation until he is cleansed, whether by the laws of purification that will come later, for one who touched a dead person or had an issue, where he was separated for a limited time, or by complete healing for one smitten with the disease of leprosy. God makes clear that the reason for their banishment is His concern that sin not be passed on to all: "that they defile not their camps." God used the expression "ye shall put out ... shall ye put out" twice in one sentence to stress the separation and not to be lax in it.

My beloved brother ... if God lives and dwells in you, then do not accept sin or the thought of it, and separate yourself from evil and the wicked so that you may save your life and not be affected by associating with them, for there is no one among us who is not affected by the atmosphere around him ... And draw nearer still to spiritual friends, so that you live in purity and cleanness.

entries.section: (1) The separation of persons and the unclean

paragraphs.text: The people obeyed all that God commanded Moses, with submission and with conviction of the duty of separating evil.

entries.section: (2) Treachery against another

paragraphs.text: The discourse moved from the separation of the defiled to another matter, which is a man's treachery against his fellow man, and this discourse comes as a completion of what is found in the Book of Leviticus (ch. 6:1-7). We note in this verse the following:
1- There is no difference between man and woman in committing any sin, for God regards everyone who sins as guilty, whatever his sex or color.

2- To commit a trespass against the Lord: that is, even if the sin is directed from one person to another or against him, the wrong is in the first place directed at God Himself and at His person directly. For this reason David the prophet says, though he had sinned by adultery against the woman with whom he committed adultery, her and her husband, "Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight" (Ps 50).
3- That soul be guilty: even if no one saw her, she is guilty and deserving of divine punishment, or of offering repentance to God and also to the one against whom she sinned.

entries.section: (2) Treachery against another

paragraphs.text: After God defined the wrong of the soul that committed treachery or theft, He explains to us here the steps of repentance and remedy as follows:

1- They shall confess their sin: that is, they offer repentance and confession first to God, and to the priest who will receive the sacrifice (v. 8), and to the one against whom they sinned. This confession, which proceeds in three directions, is beneficial for the human soul to make, because it is a harsh exposure of it, and perhaps God wanted by this to alert man to what sin will bring upon him, so that he is deterred and does not venture upon it.

This takes place now in the Church in the sacrament of confession, in which the penitent receives forgiveness of his sins, in addition to his peace of mind and the guidance he receives from the father of confession to help him not to fall.

2- He shall recompense his trespass: God is just in His judgments ... it is unreasonable for a person to take something from his brother ... and say I am sorry ... rather he must return what he stole ... And we err if we think that sin is forgiven in the sacrament of confession without the person returning what he took from his brother, for God is very clear in His words: there is no forgiveness unless you return what you took.

3- And add unto it the fifth part thereof: that is, an additional fifth on what you took or seized. This is considered a punishment for the one who took, so that a person is deterred and does not venture upon the wrong in the first place, and on the other hand it is considered compensation for the one whose right was taken, whether compensation for a material loss or for the feelings of distress that befell him when he learned of his loss or of what was taken from him, as Zacchaeus did for those from whom he had extorted their money (Lk 19:8).

entries.section: (2) Treachery against another

paragraphs.text: But if the person wronged has died and has no heir or kinsman to whom the wrongdoer may return what he took, God does not acquit the wrongdoer of his guilt except by his returning what he took. In this case, however, the restitution is made to the Lord, who is represented here by the priest responsible for applying the laws of God ... And if by this action the right returns to its owner who was wronged, or to God, there remains something else, which is to complete the apology to God Himself by offering a ram, that is, a lamb, as a sacrifice of atonement for sin, a clear indication that the blood of the sacrifice, which signifies the blood of Christ, is alone what atones for and forgives the sins of man, as the Apostle says, "without shedding of blood is no remission" (Heb 9:22).

Be faithful in your dealings with others, so that God is pleased with you and blesses you, in addition to winning the love of those around you, so that you live in peace and tranquility. This is more important than any material gains you obtain by illegitimate means or seize from others.

entries.section: (3) Some rights of the priests

paragraphs.text: Every offering: that is, the shoulder of the heave offering (the sacrifice), which was the right of the priest who performs the service (Ex 29:26-28). Of the holy things of the children of Israel: these are the vows and sacrifices offered by the people to the Lord.
Every man's hallowed things shall be his: that is, what a person offers to God, of prescribed sacrifices or vows, shall be for the priest.

In these two verses God speaks about the rights of the priests, for they are His children and His own, whom He commends to the people. And so that the people's honoring of the priest would not be a favor from them to him, God set it in the form of a law binding on the people. Everything that is offered to God, apart from the burnt offering, whether at the level of the people at the feasts or at the level of the individual as in vows, belongs to the priests' portion, as do the parts that God appointed for the priest from the peace offerings. The discourse here brings out for us the following meanings:
1- God's concern for the priests, as we pointed out.
2- Urging the people to honor them.
3- Honoring them is honoring God Himself: "He that receiveth you receiveth me" (Mt 10:40).

The priesthood in the Church of the New Testament has acquired a higher and more exalted station, since the sacrifice has become living and eternal and is no longer the blood of goats and bulls ... Likewise the responsibility of the priest has become wider in teaching, administering, guiding and shepherding. Therefore we must all pray for our fathers the priests, that God may help them in their responsibility before Him, which is the salvation of their souls and the souls of all their blessed people.

entries.section: (4) The law of jealousy and suspicion

paragraphs.text: The speech was from God to Moses, and He commanded him to tell his people the following provisions of the Law, relating to the woman who has departed from the way of truth and the law of marriage, "gone aside," and fallen into marital unfaithfulness, that is, adultery.
God's concern to expose the sin of the adulterous woman is useful for the following:
1- Establishing peace and trust between the spouses so that the family lives in tranquility.
